purpose: Proves the owner base-approval gate actually blocks a build in CI, not just in unit tests.
why_this_run_exists: The dispatch input claimed owner approval, but docs/os/DEBIAN-BASE-DECISION.json is still status=pending. This is exactly the self-assertion the old gate allowed and the new gate must refuse.

skipped_steps: 4 - Install the pinned build and validation toolchain
5 - Record the build environment and toolchain versions
6 - Build the Debian Live image (real live-build)
8 - Boot the exact built ISO under QEMU
9 - Assert the boot evidence is a real PASS

what_this_proves: A dispatcher who selects 'owner-has-approved' cannot build while the committed decision record is pending. The gate fails before any toolchain install, any live-build invocation, and any QEMU boot. No ISO was produced and no boot was attempted.
what_this_does_not_prove: It does not prove a build succeeds once the owner approves. That requires a real dispatch after the record is approved, and no such run exists yet.
